steps.say: A LiDAR spun hard up a narrow staircase. Few walls, fast turns, the case that breaks LiDAR odometry.

steps.caption: PV-LIO on the README's staircase sequence
steps.say: This is PV-LIO holding on. What it changes from FAST-LIO2 is how much it trusts each point.

scenes.headline: PV-LIO: planes with error bars
scenes.sub: FAST-LIO2's filter on VoxelMap's probabilistic map, rebuilt without ROS
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Plank! Here is how PV-LIO weighs every LiDAR point, and what happened when I ran it.

parts.note: range and bearing noise, along the normal
parts.say: Each return carries the sensor's noise: a centimetre along the beam, a tenth of a degree across it.
Each plane it hits is a fit to noisy points, so it carries an error bar too.

parts.note: FAST-LIO2 uses one constant for all
parts.say: Their sum sets how hard that residual pulls. FAST-LIO2 gives every residual the same weight.

steps.say: A return is a range and a direction. Range noise stretches it along the beam; bearing noise widens it with distance.
Then the pose's own uncertainty is added, to put the point in the world.

scenes.title: A plane per voxel, cut until flat

labels: A flat voxel keeps its plane
The rest are cut, and try again
A new point, matched in a three-sigma band
Each residual weighed by its variance

steps.say: The map is a hash of root voxels, and every voxel tries to hold one plane.
When a voxel's points are flat enough, it fits a plane and stores its six by six covariance.
When they are not, it is cut into eight, and each child tries again, down to the last layer.
A new point matches a plane only if its distance is inside three standard deviations.
Then a near, head-on return pulls hard, and a far, grazing one barely counts.

steps.caption: planes coloured by uncertainty, blue low, red high
steps.say: On a city drive the planes come out large and certain on roads and walls, small and doubtful on cars and trees.

scenes.credit: HViktorTsoi/PV-LIO README animation, the author's run

steps.caption: the author's run: PV-LIO left, FAST-LIO2 right
steps.say: The README's own side by side, in a Hilti stairwell. That is the author's run. So I ran it myself, without ROS.

scenes.title: Run it with no ROS at all

items.say: Every ROS header it includes becomes a plain struct.
A feeder hands its own main loop one message at a time, in timestamp order.
Then the shootout harness scores the poses against each dataset's reference.

scenes.title: Oxford Spires, error over 283 m
scenes.note: ATE after one SE(3) fit, my runs
scenes.say: On the Oxford walk the Hilti config is the worst of three. Swap its weights for FAST-LIO2's constant and the error halves.

scenes.label: peak memory, 0.25 m voxels, one Oxford walk
scenes.say: And the map never forgets. Quarter-metre voxels over a whole quad, kept forever, peaked near nine gigabytes.

left.title: Fixed weight
left.say: With one constant weight, the basement ties and the quad improves. But the stairwells diverge.

right.title: Weighted, as shipped
right.say: Weighted, as shipped, it is the only run that holds together in the stairwells.

scenes.text: Weighting each residual by its variance is right in principle, but its scale needs measuring.
scenes.say: Weighing each point by its uncertainty is the right idea. But the noise model is two hand-set numbers, and their scale decides how far the LiDAR outweighs the IMU.
